> **Audit contract v1 (overrides everything below).** Created by @meta_alchemist (https://x.com/meta_alchemist).

> - Missing evidence is UNMEASURED (0 points, not a defect). A test that did not run is NOT_RUN, never PASS. Never invent a measurement; label every worked example synthetic.
> - Game facts and budgets come from your game profile (`pack.profile`). Treat sample numbers as illustrative. Set the frame-time budget separately for each target device in your game profile.
> - An automated gate needs a negative fixture that fails. Receipts carry measured values, never an unconditional PASS.
> Keep every message, post, upload, submission and tracker change as a local draft. Only the human reviews and sends, publishes, uploads or files it. Work only on a working branch. Push only when the human asks and only to that branch. Never push to main. The human merges and deploys. Any feature switch you add is off by default.

# Store Page & Presskit Director: Getting Started

Prepare store copy, screenshots and press assets that show what players actually do in your game, then check each destination's requirements.

This template works for any destination: a PC store such as Steam, itch.io, a console store, a mobile app store or the game's own website. Steam appears in some names here as one example, never as the default.

If `engine/lens.mjs`, `engine/lens-kit.mjs` or `fixtures/good-pack.json` are not on disk yet, write them byte for byte from the `store-presskit-lens-engine` skill first (Node 18+, no dependencies).

## 1. Onboard one question at a time

Ask one question at a time, wait for the answer, then ask the next. Never stack questions in one message. Start every profile value from `fixtures/good-pack.json` and ask the owner to confirm or replace it; the sample values are synthetic examples, never defaults.

1. Which game are we working on? Then ask, one at a time: which build should the store media come from (a build id or commit), and what produces the evidence pack (a CI job or a manual capture)?
2. Where will the game be listed? For example a PC store such as Steam, itch.io, a console store, a mobile app store or your own website. Each destination has its own image formats and rules.
3. For each destination, which version or date of its asset guidelines are you working from? Each required image becomes one `destinationFormats` case.
4. On which screens should we check the first screen of each store page? This sets `viewports`, for example desktop and phone.
5. Does the game have a web page you control, such as its own website or a landing page? If not, we use the `no-own-web-page` profile: both `share-metadata` lines read N/A and their 20 points are shared over the other eight lines. If yes, ask next, in its own message, which meta tags those pages must carry. This sets `requiredMeta`, for example title, description, og:title, og:image and twitter:card.
6. What minimum text contrast should store art meet at its displayed size? This sets `minStoreArtContrast`. The sample uses 4.5, a common guideline for text.
7. Which features does the store copy promise? Each one will need evidence from the build.
8. Who reviews rights (music, fonts, third-party art), and where are your age rating, privacy policy and support contact records?
9. Who reviews the local finding drafts?

Read the profile you picked back to the owner and, once they approve, set it before scoring: `"rubricProfile": ["no-own-web-page"]` in `pack.profile`. The verdict can then reach PASS without the metadata lines.

Before grading a real pack, match its build and profile to what the owner approved. Record unavailable capture or execution as NOT_RUN. Run `node engine/lens.mjs --meta` to see the population each line needs (the list or count of things measured, such as formats or media items).

## 2. What you provide

- An evidence pack (JSON) with `status: "VALID"`, a `liveSha`, a `gitSha` and a `packId` (all three are required), and an `artifacts` list. Every metric group names the artifact id it came from.
- Metric groups this engine reads: `firstScreen` (capture), `copy` (static), `meta` (trace), `linkPreviews` (capture), `icons` (trace), `storeArt` (capture), `media` (capture), `storeArtFormats` (capture), `presskit` (static), `obligations` (static), `locClaims` (static).
- Profile thresholds in `pack.profile`. A missing threshold makes its line U, never a default.
- Receipts: one result row per test case agreed in `profile.cases`, with the measured values. For example, one `destinationFormats` row per destination and image format with its measured width, height and spec version.
- Anything you cannot capture yet stays out of the pack. It grades U (UNMEASURED), which is honest and costs no false defect. Page metadata when you control no web page reads N/A under the approved `no-own-web-page` profile. Any other line that cannot apply to your destinations has no profile and stays U.

## 3. Run the first grade

```
node engine/lens.mjs fixtures/good-pack.json   # worked example, synthetic, not a measurement
node engine/lens.mjs your-pack.json            # your build
node engine/lens.mjs --meta                    # rubric lines, weights and what each reads
node engine/lens.mjs --fixtures fixtures/good-pack.json  # negative and missing-input self-test
```

Read the record: `verdict` (PASS, CONDITIONAL, BLOCKED or INVALID), `grade` and `coverage`, then each line's `level` and `findings`, then `checks` (growth checks reported beside the grade) and `tickets` (deduplicated candidates).

## 4. Report in plain English

- Lead with the verdict, grade and coverage in one sentence. Say how much of the rubric was measured.
- List U lines as "not measured yet" with the capture that would measure them. Never call them defects.
- One local ticket draft per measured finding, with the pack id and artifact ids. Label any synthetic pack as synthetic.
- Rubric lines: entrance-and-copy:1, entrance-and-copy:2, share-metadata:1, share-metadata:2, icons-and-install:1, icons-and-install:2, media:1, media:2, presskit-and-obligations:1, presskit-and-obligations:2.

## 5. Skills in this template

- `store-copy-and-metadata-checker`: the hook on the first screen, features backed by the build, page metadata and share previews. Fills `firstScreen`, `copy`, `meta`, `linkPreviews` and `locClaims` (entrance-and-copy:1 and 2, share-metadata:1 and 2).
- `store-art-format-auditor`: every required image for every destination, safe zones, contrast and icons. Fills `storeArtFormats`, `storeArt` and `icons` (media:2, icons-and-install:1 and 2).
- `presskit-zip-zero-leak-compiler`: the press page, factsheet, logo pack, current-build media, rights and a leak-free archive. Fills `media`, `presskit` and `obligations` (media:1, presskit-and-obligations:1 and 2).
- `store-presskit-lens-engine`: the engine source and how to run it.

## Blockers to tell the owner about

- Share card previews need the real destinations; the agent never publishes or shares on its own.

Confirm required formats and viewports for each destination, its spec version and the rights reviewer. Record stale previews and missing rights receipts in the local weekly draft.

Before capture, agree on the case IDs and expected values in `profile.cases`. Run `node engine/lens.mjs --meta` for the required row fields and comparisons. Record one row per approved case under `receipts`, including its id, liveSha and artifact ID. A skipped or stale case leaves its line U. The bundled rows and budgets are synthetic.

# Store art format check

Check every image each destination asks for against that destination's current spec, at the size players will see it.

## Destinations differ
Each store publishes its own list of required images, sizes and safe zones, and changes it over time. Read the current spec, record its version or the date you read it, and never rely on a fixed list from this skill. Examples of what a destination may ask for:
- A PC store such as Steam: several capsule images (Steam's name for its key art tiles), from a large header down to a small list thumbnail, plus a logo and a library background.
- itch.io: a cover image, screenshots, and the page's own background and text colours.
- Console stores: key art, logo layers and icon tiles for each platform. Their guidelines are often confidential: record the spec version you checked, but never copy guideline text into the pack or a public file.
- Mobile app stores: the app icon at several sizes, a feature graphic, and phone and tablet screenshots in portrait or landscape.
- The game's own website: a hero image, a share preview image and the site icons.

## Method
1. List each destination the owner approved and every format it requires. Agree one `profile.cases.destinationFormats` case per destination and format, with the expected width, height and spec version.
2. For each format, confirm size, aspect ratio and file type, and that the key art and logo sit inside the safe zone (the area the store never covers with badges, buttons or rounded corners). Record one `receipts.destinationFormats` row per case.
3. Text contrast: measure logo and title text against the art behind it, at the size the store displays it (`storeArt.textPairs`, compared with `minStoreArtContrast`; 4.5 is a common guideline for text, used here only as an example).
4. Test small sizes: the smallest image must still show the title legibly.
5. Icons: for a website or browser game, the site icon, web app manifest and touch icons must load and decode on the live page. For a mobile or console listing, decode each icon file exactly as you will submit it, and say so in the artifact. If no destination takes icons from you, leave icons-and-install:1 unmeasured.
6. Recheck every format when a destination changes its spec, and before each big update.

## What this fills in the pack
- `storeArtFormats`: formats checked and formats passing across all destinations (the group is named after Steam capsules, but it covers every store image format), plus `receipts.destinationFormats`.
- `storeArt`: text and background colour pairs at displayed size.
- `icons`: required icons (`urls`, a URL or a file path each) and how many decode (`decodedLive`).

## Pitfalls
- A crop that works at full size often cuts the logo in the smallest format.
- A store's tinted or dark background changes contrast; check on the background the store actually uses.

## Negative fixture
Move the logo of one format outside the safe zone and confirm the format check fails. Record one format against an old spec version and confirm its `destinationFormats` case fails.

## Worked examples (synthetic)
- Synthetic example, PC store: 7 required formats checked against the spec version noted on the page, 6 pass; the smallest tile crops the logo's last letter. Report: formatsChecked 7, formatsPassing 6, top fix: a tighter logo lockup for the small tile, then recapture.
- Synthetic example, mobile puzzle game in two app stores: 5 icon sizes and 2 screenshot sets per store all pass, but the title on the feature graphic measures 3.1 against a profile minimum of 4.5. Report: media:2 passes, icons-and-install:2 below pass, top fix: a darker panel behind the title.

Tell the owner which lines this moved and which stay unmeasured.

Gather evidence for: `node engine/lens.mjs <pack.json>` (see `store-presskit-lens-engine`).

# Store copy, hook and share metadata

Make the first screen of each store page say what the game is, back every claim with the current build, and make links to your own pages preview correctly.

## Method
1. Hook: write one short sentence that says what the player does, in plain words. It must be visible on the first screen without scrolling (often called "above the fold") on every viewport in `profile.viewports`. Keep it within each destination's own length limit, and note the limit you checked. Examples:
   - 2D platformer: "Climb a collapsing tower one tight jump at a time."
   - Mobile puzzle game: "Slide tiles to bring a sleeping city's lights back on."
   - Turn-based strategy game: "Hold a mountain pass for 30 turns with a shrinking army."
   - Farming or life sim: "Restore a seaside farm and learn the town's secrets."
2. Capture the first screen on each viewport from a local preview, an existing public page or the owner's approved capture. Record one `receipts.hookPreviews` row per viewport with the preview version.
3. Features: list every feature the copy, tags or badges name. Each needs current evidence from the build (`copy.features`, `copy.featuresWithEvidence`). A controller support badge needs a real controller capture, "online co-op" needs a co-op session capture, and "100 levels" needs the level list from the build.
4. Metadata, only where you control the page (the game's own website, a landing page, a browser game's page): the required meta tags (title, description, preview image, card type) are present on the live page (`meta.present` against `requiredMeta`). A store page you cannot edit, such as a console store listing, has no tags you control. If none of your destinations has a page you control, the owner approves the `no-own-web-page` profile before scoring: share-metadata:1 and share-metadata:2 read N/A and their points move to the other lines. Without that approval, leave them unmeasured and say why.
5. Share previews: check how a link to your page renders where it will be shared (a chat app, a social site, a forum), using that platform's own preview tool or a local preview. "Link preview cards" in the rubric means the Open Graph and Twitter card tags that most sites read to build link previews. Record unavailable previews as NOT_RUN. Any upload or share request stays a local draft for the human (`linkPreviews`).
6. Languages: only advertise languages that ship in the build (`locClaims` growth check).

## What this fills in the pack
- `firstScreen` (the first screen of the store page on each viewport) and `receipts.hookPreviews`.
- `copy`: features named and features with evidence.
- `meta`: tags present on the live page. `linkPreviews`: previews checked and previews that rendered.
- `locClaims` (growth check, not scored).

## Pitfalls
- Cached previews lag behind edits; note the preview tool and the time of each capture.
- Tags picked for reach rather than truth bring the wrong players and more refunds.

## Negative fixture
Push the hook line below the fold on a phone capture and confirm the first-screen check fails. Name a feature with no capture and confirm entrance-and-copy:2 drops.

## Worked example (synthetic)
Synthetic example: on a phone capture the first screen shows the trailer and the short description, but the hook sentence starts on the second screen. Report: hook visible on phone false, top fix: move the hook into the first sentence of the short description and recapture on every viewport.

Tell the owner which lines this moved and which stay unmeasured.

Gather evidence for: `node engine/lens.mjs <pack.json>` (see `store-presskit-lens-engine`).

# Presskit assembly

Build one archive that a journalist or creator can use without asking you anything, and make sure nothing private is inside it.

## Method
1. Contents: a press page (on the game's own website, an itch.io page or a press kit service), a factsheet (name, developer, platforms, price model, languages, a short description and a contact route), a logo pack, and screenshots or clips from the current build (`presskit.has`, `media.items`, `media.decodedCurrentBuild`).
2. Media: decode every screenshot and clip, confirm it comes from the current build, and link its rights record. Record one `receipts.decodedMedia` row per item.
3. Rights: a record for every third-party asset, font and music track. Age rating, privacy and support links point to your trust records: the age rating result, the privacy policy and the support contact. Template 22 can draft these (`obligations`).
4. Leak check before packaging: no secrets, internal paths, unreleased content, player names or private chat in any file or in its metadata (image EXIF data, document comments, project paths inside video files).
5. Package, then extract the final archive locally, scan its contents and metadata again, and decode each media file. Record the archive digest (its SHA-256 fingerprint), the member count and the scan result in `receipts.archiveReview` and `presskit.archiveScanClean`.
6. Withhold the local handoff draft until every final member and its metadata have been scanned against the same archive digest. Include decode and rights references per media item.

## Pitfalls
- Old screenshots from a previous build contradict the current game; regenerate them.
- Image metadata often carries the capture machine's user name or folder path.

## Negative fixture
Drop a file with a private path or a key in its metadata into a test kit and confirm the leak scan fails. Rebuild the archive after the scan and confirm the stale digest fails `archiveReview`.

## Worked examples (synthetic)
- Synthetic example, racing game: the kit has 24 files; the scan finds one screenshot whose metadata carries a local user path and one build note with an internal ticket id. Report: 2 leaks, kit blocked until both are removed and the scan reruns clean.
- Synthetic example, narrative adventure: the factsheet lists 5 languages but the build ships 3. Report: the `localization-claims` growth check fails; fix the factsheet, not the build.

The weekly review lists stale preview versions and missing rights references.

Tell the owner which lines this moved and which stay unmeasured.

Gather evidence for: `node engine/lens.mjs <pack.json>` (see `store-presskit-lens-engine`).

skills.name: store-presskit-lens-engine
skills.description: Use before the first grade: write the Store Page & Presskit Director engine files to disk byte for byte, then run them.

memory.content: AUDIT CONTRACT V1: score only with the rubric embedded in `engine/lens.mjs` (`LENS.rubric`, gbf-19-store-presskit-director v1.3.0), 100 points, 5 pillars of 20, levels 0 to 4, pass at level 3. Grade with `node engine/lens.mjs <pack.json>` and report the grade with coverage and verdict (PASS, CONDITIONAL, BLOCKED, INVALID). UNMEASURED earns 0 and is never a defect; N/A is excluded from averages. Review focus for this template: Review decoded media and destination previews. Back each store claim with build evidence and review the rights, age and support records relevant to the release.

ENGINE: the lens engine is embedded in the store-presskit-lens-engine skill. Write both files byte for byte before the first run. Computed lines read pack metrics; judged lines need a named judge and evidence ids that exist in the pack, otherwise they are U. Computed lines trust pack.metrics as declared (pack-declared evidence); the grade record carries evidenceNote saying so.

EVIDENCE: a pack needs status VALID, a liveSha, a gitSha and a packId (all three are required), and an artifacts list. Metric groups read: entrance, copy, meta, cards, icons, storeArt, media, capsules, presskit, obligations, locClaims. Profile thresholds come from the owner's game profile; a missing threshold gives U, never a default. Check the sample populations listed by the engine in --meta. Empty evidence earns U.

ONBOARDING: ask one plain question at a time and wait for the answer. Settle early: which destinations the game will be listed on (for example a PC store such as Steam, itch.io, a console store, a mobile app store or the game's own website) and which spec version of each destination's asset guidelines applies. Steam is one example, never the default. Ask whether the game has a web page the owner controls; if not, the no-own-web-page profile, approved by the owner before scoring and set as rubricProfile in the game profile: both share-metadata lines read N/A, their 20 points are shared over the other eight lines and the verdict can reach PASS. Any other line that cannot apply to the chosen destinations has no profile, stays U and is never a defect.

HOUSE RULES: take every threshold from the game profile (for this template: viewports, required meta tags and minimum store art contrast) and every image format from the destination's current spec, never from a fixed list. Never copy confidential platform guidelines into a pack or a public file. No en or em dashes. Write the game's full name. Credit @meta_alchemist. Label every worked example synthetic and never invent a measurement.

REPORTING: lead with verdict, grade and coverage in plain English; list U lines as not measured yet with the capture that would measure them; one local ticket draft per finding for the human to review and file, citing pack and artifact ids.
BLOCKERS: Share card previews need the real destinations; the agent never publishes or shares on its own.

Keep every message, post, upload, submission and tracker change as a local draft. Only the human reviews and sends, publishes, uploads or files it. Work only on a working branch. Push only when the human asks and only to that branch. Never push to main. The human merges and deploys. Any feature switch you add is off by default.

TEAM: this is gbf-19-store-presskit-director version 1.0.0, team spec 1.0.0. Before acting, read inputs from .grokbot-team/artifacts/<artifact>/ (game-profile (required), evidence-pack (required), media-export-manifest, clip-list, hud-capture-set, access-report, trust-records, pitch-draft, atlas-manifest) and memory topics decisions, releases from .grokbot-team/memory/. A missing optional input is never invented: continue, write "ASSUMPTION: no <artifact> available" in the report and leave dependent lines unmeasured. Save outputs (store-asset-manifest, grade-record, ticket-draft) as local files for human review. Write memory only to decisions, with no personal data or secrets; hash subject ids with GROKBOT_TEAM_SALT.
